unmapped_findings: For the intermediate-Al alloy Fe-30Mn-1.2C-2Al (2 wt.% Al), aging has a much smaller influence on tensile behavior than for the Al-free alloy (weakening/embrittlement) and the 8 wt.% Al alloy (strengthening); its properties fall between the 0Al and 8Al behaviors [b0024, b0025].
With 30 wt.% Mn and 2 wt.% Al (≤4–5 wt.% Al), the TWIP effect prevails as the deformation mechanism, placing this sample in the SIMPLEX (single-phase austenitic TWIP) steel class [b0031].

Pronounced j-carbide (κ-carbide) formation/strengthening is associated in the paper with aging at 500–600 °C or with higher Al content (Al > 10 wt.% forming during quenching); the 450 °C/1 h, 2 wt.% Al condition of this sample is outside that stated regime [b0031, b0109].

Fig. 3 presents mechanical data for 45 material conditions of the Fe-30Mn-1.2C base composition; the 450 °C/1 h aging condition is drawn as the blue curve, but no printed per-condition numeric values at 2 wt.% Al are given in the text (only axis-level approximate ranges) [b0022, figure_003].
